title: definition.locked@10
description: A definition of done was locked: its hash, the issue's revision and the base commit, each requirement with its author (marked automated when its work source's reading says so), its check's approved bytes by digest, the expected outputs its check references by digest, the command its check runs where the check isn't a drafted file, the criterion ID it quotes, the surface its check declares it enters through, and the targets it names (#323). Only the core appends it. @7 (#325): a requirement whose check costs money says what it spends on, `paid`, so the lock prices it. Since @8, a requirement may name the clean runs it needs and its held-out variants (#1018). @9 (#352): a requirement whose check is a timing check says so, `timing`, so a run of it that fails under load is rerun alone. @10 (#1331): a requirement only the scheduled budget window can settle says so, `settled_by: "budget-window"`, and has no check: it never holds a landing, and its task stays open naming it until the window closes it.

subject.description: The record object this event is about.

writer.description: Only the core appends this kind.

actor.description: The person behind it, from the credential.

seq.description: Order within the session: ns since the epoch when the hook started.

log_pos.description: Its position in the event log, assigned by the hub at append.

task_ref.description: The task: a task handle, or the message that asked for it (session:<id>#<message>).

source_line.description: The line of text the requirement came from: ask#L<n> for a line of the prompt, <source_id>#L<n> for a line of a work item.

refuted_by.description: The observation that would refute it, so it can fail.

check.description: The check that judges it, a path in the repo; null for a requirement left without one.

check_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the check's bytes as approved at the lock, kept by digest in the hub; null with no check, or a check that wasn't there.

on_base.description: What its check must do on the base commit.

x-closure.closed: each value is a state the record defines and every reader acts on, so a value outside the list has no meaning

asserts.description: The assertions in its check that carry the requirement, by file and line, step ID or deadline.

oracle.description: Who judges it: code, a model or a person.

x-closure.closed: each value is a state the record defines and every reader acts on, so a value outside the list has no meaning
x-closure.reopens: a new major of this schema

near_misses.description: For a requirement without a check: the existing checks that came closest, and why each falls short.

author.description: Who wrote the text it came from, with the role their work source's work.item@1 reading gives them, never one read from the text.

role.description: you for your prompt; otherwise the work source's membership record.

x-closure.closed: each value is a state the record defines and every reader acts on, so a value outside the list has no meaning
x-closure.reopens: a new major of this schema

automated.description: True when the work source's reading marks the author automated (an app or a bot account): their text counts as outside text whatever their membership.

expected_ms.description: How long its check is expected to take, in milliseconds: what admits it to a lane.

deadline_ms.description: How long its check may take, in milliseconds, past which its run times out.

surface.description: The surface its check declares it enters through, for a stand-in on a base with nothing to start: a JSON service's routes, a page's routes, a command's name, or a module's path and exports; null for none.

kind.description: service, page, command or module have a fixed form; any other kind goes to the early question.

references.description: The expected outputs the check references, each kept by digest at the lock as the check's bytes are, so the hash covers them and the claim's run gets the approved bytes.

command.description: The command the check runs where the check is one of the repo's own tests rather than a drafted file under .deepbuild/, such as the test runner on a file tagged with the criterion's ID.

criterion.description: The acceptance criterion's ID where the requirement quotes one, #<issue>.<first 8 hex of the SHA-256 of its text>.

targets.description: The stable names its check targets (#323), each resolved in the claim's snapshot before its runs: a file and the symbol it defines, <file>#<symbol>. One that doesn't resolve makes the claim INVALID.

paid.description: What its check spends money on, when it costs any: a live call, a hosted browser run or a model job.

x-closure.closed: each value is a kind of spend the budget prices, and the lock acts on each
x-closure.reopens: a new major of this schema

runs.description: How many clean runs its check needs; one when absent.

held_out.description: Its check's held-out variants: each the files written over the claim's checkout for a run of its own, kept by digest and never sent to the agent.

timing.description: Its check is a timing check: a run that fails while the machine's load is past its core count is rerun alone once, and the rerun decides.

settled_by.description: What alone can settle it, when no check of the claim can: the scheduled budget window (#1116), which measures the merged commit on a reference Mac. Such a requirement has no check; it never holds a landing, and the task stays open naming it.

x-closure.closed: each value is a settler the design names (Landing in turn); a requirement any check settles has none
x-closure.reopens: a new major of this schema

deliverables.description: What the work must deliver, each a path or a name.

issue_rev.description: The issue's revision the definition was drafted from: a work item's updated time, or the prompt's digest for a message.
